subject: Urgent: spike in TLS RTT causing p99 latency regressions for Acme Toys
messages:
From: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh@acmetoys.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: ops@acmetoys.com
Date: 2026-10-28T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Latency spike — many sessions hitting p99 on first byte

Stephanie,

We're seeing a big customer impact this morning — p95/p99 for initial responses from the Hosted API to our EU and US users jumped ~2–3x starting ~07:50 PDT. It manifests as delayed page loads and failed checkout steps; our metrics show many requests timing out on the client after ~5s.

I've attached a sample trace bundle (acme_tls_traces.zip) and a screenshot of the SLO dashboard. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side? Our infra team saw elevated TCP/TLS RTTs to the CDN edge and some TLS timeouts on retries.

This is critical for our holiday campaign. Please escalate if needed — Rajesh

--
Rajesh Gupta
Director of Engineering, Acme Toys
rajesh@acmetoys.com
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh@acmetoys.com>, ops@acmetoys.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-28T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike — many sessions hitting p99 on first byte

Rajesh —

Thank you for the traces and the heads up. I'm escalating internally and copying our infra and SRE leads. Initial read: the symptom set (elevated TLS handshake/RTT + CDN edge errors) points to an upstream edge/CDN degradation rather than model runtime.

Immediate ask from our side: can you confirm the affected origins/IP blocks and whether requests are routed through any customer-managed cache rules? We'll parallel-run a trace from our edge to your origin and loop in the CDN provider.

Marissa / Jonas — can you start a cross-check on our edge->upstream TLS RTTs and identify any sudden certificate or TLS library changes in the last 24 hours? Jonas — please also surface any recent ACL or route changes.

I'll update Rajesh and bring in Platform leadership if we see cross-customer impact.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-28T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike — many sessions hitting p99 on first byte

Stephanie —

I've pulled the edge metrics. Between 07:45–08:10 PDT we see a spike in TLS handshake timeouts and increased SYN->ACK delays for the egress cluster serving Acme's CIDR. Per-host RTTs to the CDN edge increased by ~250–400ms on average; a subset retried and succeeded, causing extra queued work and higher p99s. No recent cert rotation from us.

I opened a ticket with the CDN partner (ticket #CDN-9871) and attached the sample traces you forwarded. Attaching the SLO snapshot here (slo_p99_dashboard.png).

Next steps: 1) get CDN provider to confirm if they saw regional edge saturation / backend connection storms; 2) temporarily route Acme through an alternate POP if they allow it; 3) monitor for TLS-level retransmits.

-Marissa

Attachments: slo_p99_dashboard.png
From: Marta Lopez <marta@edgeprovider.net>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-28T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed RTT spikes — investigating upstream backend connections

Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks for the traces. We are seeing anomalous connection churn from a small set of PoPs starting 07:40 PDT in the west-us region; TLS handshake retry counts increased and keepalive connections to some origins were reset due to a buggy route flap in one of our edge clusters. We've isolated the affected cluster and are draining it; the mitigation should complete in ~30–45 minutes.

We will provide a post-mitigation correlation report and a pcap snippet. In the meantime, if you can toggle routing for Acme to an alternate PoP, that will reduce their p99 quickly.

Regards,
Marta Lopez
Edge Operations, EdgeProvider Net
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike — many sessions hitting p99 on first byte

Quick update:

1) I validated that our TLS config and cert chains are unchanged and healthy. No libssl upgrades deployed in the last 48 hours.
2) Rolling a targeted route change for Acme to route through us-west-2 alternate PoPs is prepared; awaiting approval from Stephanie to execute (risk: short flow changes, potential transient sessions dropped).
3) I recommend we also enable short-circuiting prefix cache for Acme (bypass one layer of CDN) for 2 hours to observe SLOs.

If Stephanie approves, I'll coordinate the route change with the CDN provider and notify Acme.

-Jonas
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh@acmetoys.com>, Marta Lopez <marta@edgeprovider.net>
Date: 2026-10-28T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike — many sessions hitting p99 on first byte

Team / Rajesh —

Thanks for the quick triage and to Marta for the isolation work. Jonas, go ahead with the targeted route move to the alternate PoP and enable the prefix bypass for Acme for the next 2 hours. Coordinate with Marta before the cut (I want a rollback window). Marissa, monitor p95/p99 and error rate closely and escalate to Platform if we see any model-side queuing impact.

Rajesh, we'll keep you updated every 30 minutes during the cut. Our goal is to bring p99 close to baseline within the maintenance window. I know this is high-impact for your campaign — we'll prioritize accordingly.

Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

--Forwarded message attached: sample traces (acme_tls_traces.zip)
